subject: Security

findings.subject: Security
findings.title: No authentication scheme is registered anywhere in the application; every endpoint is explicitly anonymous
findings.recommendation: Register an authentication scheme (e.g. JWT bearer or API key) via builder.Services.AddAuthentication(...), and remove [AllowAnonymous] from state-changing endpoints such as /v1/testing/reset.

findings.subject: Security
findings.title: The destructive testing-data-reset endpoint has no authorization check
findings.recommendation: Require an authenticated caller with an explicit role/scope (e.g. an 'admin' or 'test-automation' policy) for POST /v1/testing/reset, since it deletes production-shaped data.

checkResults.subject: Security
checkResults.reason: No AddAuthentication/authentication middleware is configured anywhere; both controllers are [AllowAnonymous].

checkResults.subject: Security
checkResults.reason: No authorization policy guards the data-mutating reset endpoint.

checkResults.subject: Security
checkResults.reason: No session cookies or server-side sessions are used; the API is stateless with no auth mechanism at all.

checkResults.subject: Security
checkResults.reason: The application does not store end-user passwords; only DB connection credentials appear in config (covered under Security — Operational).

checkResults.subject: Security

checkResults.subject: Security
checkResults.reason: With no authentication at all, access relies entirely on network-level trust rather than explicit per-request verification.

notes: This is a small proof-of-concept API; both endpoints are intentionally anonymous today. Flagged because a destructive data-reset endpoint with no auth is a real risk if ever exposed outside a fully trusted network.
